toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B looks fine. One Level 2 potassium QC result failed. The other two levels passed, and sodium and chloride passed in the same run. A re-poured repeat passed 21 minutes later. That is consistent with a chance flag, since this rule gives about one or two a month at your volume, or with a one-off sampling glitch. The evidence can't tell those two apart, so don't record a glitch as the confirmed cause. QC ran on schedule, so the short-staffing theory doesn't hold. Level 2 means are the same before and after the lot change. Analyzer A gave the same results as B on 43 re-tested samples, within 0.10 mmol/L, and B's patient median is unchanged. The lot is not implicated.

Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between A and B. Most of them had samples in transit more than 3 hours, after the tube outage began. Renal overflow patients are a second possible explanation. Delayed transport is likely a contributor, but this is association only.

Sign off: return B to service, close the 186 flagged results with no amendments, and don't recall, quarantine or widen limits. Add temporary extra Level 2 QC for a week. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples on the high results and fix the tube station. I'm fairly confident, though not certain.
